parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ahtadak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *-ašta-.
From Proto-Finnic *-t'ak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *-te-.

parole.significato: Forms nouns, mainly bird names (in dialects) and some toponyms.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-nka, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *-nka.

parole.significato: Forms some nouns, mainly clippings and in slang.
parole.testo: Possibly from Proto-Finnic *-ppa, from Proto-Finno-Permic *-ppa, but the narrow distribution and rarity means this is highly uncertain. At least in slang the suffix may instead be a more recent labialized form of -kka.
From Proto-Finnic *-s, from Proto-Finno-Permic *-kse (compare Erzya and Moksha -кс (-ks, nominalizing suffix)).

parole.significato: Forms certain adverbs, typically of manner.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-tta, from Proto-Finno-Permic *-kta.

From Proto-Finnic *ahtëra, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *akšterɜ, but in any case potentially borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian [Term?] (compare Sanskrit अक्षेत्र (ákṣetra, “destitute of fields, uncultivated”)) Akin to Erzya якстерь (jaksteŕ).

parole.significato: to shoot, fire (fire a projectile or a weapon that fires a projectile)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ampudak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *ampe-. Probably cognate to Erzya аволдамс (avoldams, “to swing”).

parole.significato: to plead, beg, ask, request, implore, entreat, petition, solicit
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *anodak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *ana- (compare Erzya анамс (anams, “to ask, beg”)).

parole.significato: to make it, arrive or reach (in time or before something else happens)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ehtidäk (compare Estonian ehtima), from Proto-Finno-Permic *ešte- (“to make, prepare; to get ready, prepare; to ripen”) (compare Northern Sami astat, Eastern Mari ышташ (yštaš), Komi-Zyrian эштыны (eštyny), the last of these possibly borrowed from Finnic). The shift to the current

parole.significato: life (state of being alive, existence of a person or creature; experience of living, description of (a person's) day-to…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *elämä, from Proto-Finno-Permic *elämä, equivalent to elää (“to live”) + -mä.
From Proto-Finnic *hakci, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *šakče. Cognates include Erzya чакш (čakš).

parole.significato: ghost, spirit (disembodied soul; the soul or spirit of a deceased person; a spirit appearing after death)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *haamu. Cognates include Karelian huamu, Votic aamo, and dialectal Finnish hahmo, haamo, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *šamɜ. Other cognates include Erzya чама (čama, “face”), Moksha шама (šama, “face”).

From Proto-Finnic *hap'oin (compare Estonian hapu), from Proto-Finno-Permic *šappa (compare Erzya чапамо (čapamo), Moksha шапама (šapama), Eastern Mari шопо (šopo)). The declension has been levelled to a plain m-stem with two variants happama- and happame- (see usage notes below for original dialect

From Proto-Finnic *hek, from Proto-Finno-Permic *sej (compare Northern Sami sii, Erzya сынь (sïń), Northern Khanty [script needed] (ᴧĭw)). The word is inflected as plural, but there is no plural marker in the nominative, except in dialects (het). See hän for more details on history of usage.

parole.significato: sleeve, arm (part of a piece of clothing that covers the arm)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hiha, probably from earlier Proto-Finno-Permic *(š)iša. Cognates include Proto-Samic *sësē, Erzya and Moksha ожа (oža).

parole.significato: to grind, sharpen, whet (make sharper by rubbing against something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hijodak (compare Estonian ihuma, Livonian jõ’vvõ, Veps hijoda), from Proto-Finno-Permic *šiŋa- (compare Northern Sami sadjit (“to hone, file”), Skolt Sami sââjjad (“to hone, grind, file”), Erzya човамс (čovams), Moksha шовамс (šovams, “to hone, file, grind”), Eastern Mari шумем (š

From Proto-Finnic *humar (compare Estonian uhmer), from Proto-Finno-Permic *šu(š)mar ~ *šuwar (compare Erzya човар (čovar), Eastern Mari шуар (šuar)). The medial -h- is irregular and might have developed through an itself irregular lengthening of the -u- vowel.
From Proto-Finnic *hoi ~ *hui, from Proto-Finno-Permic *šoje ~ *šuje.
From Proto-Finnic *hupa, from Proto-Finno-Permic *šupa (compare Erzya чова (čova), Moksha шуваня (šuvanä, “thin”), Eastern Mari шуэ (šue)).

parole.significato: to rinse, wash (to move by the force of water in motion)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *huhtodak (compare Ingrian huuhtoa, Livonian ū’dõ), from Proto-Finno-Permic *šukštɜ- (compare Erzya кштамс (kštams), Moksha штамс (štams)).
From Proto-Finnic *hühmä, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *šɜšmɜ. Compare Erzya шушмо (šušmo, “snowbank”).

Haplologically from earlier inhiminen (compare inhimillinen), from Proto-Finnic *inhiminen (compare Estonian inimene, Karelian ihmini), possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *jenše (compare Erzya инже (inže, “guest”)); alternative explanations also exist.
From Proto-Finnic *istudak (compare Karelian istuo, Estonian istuma, Ludian ištuda), possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *isɜ- (compare Erzya озамс (ozams)).

parole.significato: to manage, to get by, to have strength, energy, or stamina
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jaksadak (compare Estonian jaksama), from Proto-Finno-Permic *jaksa- / *jëksa- (“to untie, to unfasten; to take off (clothes)”) (compare Erzya юксемс (juksems, “untie”), Udmurt юскыны (juskyny)).

parole.significato: to grind, mill, crush (reduce to smaller pieces, especially by lateral crushing motions)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jauhadak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *jaŋša- (compare Erzya яжамс (jažams)).

parole.significato: who, which, that (referring to the previous word or phrase; see usage notes)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *joka (compare Karelian joka, Votic jõka), from Proto-Finno-Permic *jo (compare Northern Sami juohkẹ, juogọ, Erzya ю- (ju-) in юза-тоза (juza-toza, “back and forth”), Eastern Mari южо (južo, “some”), Western Mari юж (juž, “some”)). The nominative and genitive singular forms, which

parole.significato: swan (any bird in the genus Cygnus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jouc'ën (compare Karelian joučen), probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *joŋkće (compare Northern Sami njukča, Erzya локсей (loksej), Moksha локсти (loksti), Eastern Mari йӱксӧ (jüksö), Komi-Permyak юсь (juś)); see the Proto-Finnic entry for more.

From Proto-Finnic *jumala (compare Estonian jumal (“god”)), from Proto-Finno-Permic *juma(-la) (“sky, god”), probably borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *dyumā (compare Sanskrit द्युम्न (dyumna, “splendor”), Sanskrit द्युमत् (dyumat, “bright; an epithet of Indra”)) or earlier Indo-European.
Inessive singular of jumi-, from Proto-Finnic *juma-, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *juma-.

parole.significato: plot, scheme, conspiracy, intrigue, stratagem; ploy, ruse (secret plan to achieve an end, the end or means usually bein…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jooni (“path”) (compare Estonian joon), from Proto-Finno-Permic *jëne (compare Southern Sami joene (“road”), Erzya ян (jan, “path”)), probably borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *yáHnam. Sense diversification from original “path” is particular to Finnic. Compare dialectal juntu (“pa
From Proto-Finnic *jäkälä, probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *jäkälä ~ *jekäl.
From Proto-Finnic *jämedä (compare Estonian jäme, Votic jämmiä), from Proto-Finno-Permic *jämä-.

From Proto-Finnic *jäsen (compare Estonian jäse), from Proto-Finno-Permic *jäsene (“joint”) (compare Erzya эзне (ezne, “joint”) and Udmurt ёз (joz, “joint”)). * (member (part of a group, etc.)): Probably a semantic loan from another language, compare German Glied (“limb”) → Mitglied (“member”). * (t

parole.significato: lid, top, cover (generally flat cover of a hole or a container such as a jar or a box)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kanci (compare Estonian kaas), from Proto-Finno-Permic *kamte (compare Northern Sami goavdi, Erzya кундо (kundo, “lid”), Eastern Mari комдыш (komdyš)).

parole.significato: to escape, run away, flee, fly, get away (from captivity)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kargait'ak (compare Estonian kargama (“to jump, hop”), Livonian kargõ (“to jump”), Ludian kargaita (“to run”), Veps kargata (“to dance”)), possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *karka- (compare Erzya кра- (kra-) in кравтомс (kravtoms, “to drive away, drive out, oust”)).

From Proto-Finnic *karkëda, probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *karke. * (unrefined): A semantic loan from other European languages; compare French gros, German grob. The antonym hieno (“fine; refined”) is likewise similarly semantically informed by other languages.

parole.significato: char, that has been burned and charred
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karci, probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *karte-.
From Proto-Finnic *kasvadak (compare Estonian kasvama, Livonian ka’zzõ, Votic kazva), from Proto-Finno-Permic *kaswa- (compare Erzya касомс (kasoms)).

parole.significato: fume(s) (strong, unpleasant and stinging smell caused by something burning)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kacku, from Proto-Finno-Permic *kačka- (“to bite”), the same root as in katkera.

From Proto-Finnic *kecrä (compare Estonian keder, North Karelian kesrä, Veps kezr), from Proto-Finno-Permic *kečrä, borrowed from early Proto-Indo-Iranian *ketstram (later *čatstram). Cognates include Erzya штере (štere).

parole.significato: The white surface layer of the bark of a birch.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kelmeh, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *kelmä.

parole.significato: ball, clew (quantity of string, thread, etc., wound into a spherical shape)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kerä (compare Estonian kera, Livonian kierā, Votic čerä), from Proto-Finno-Permic *kerä (compare Erzya кире (kire)).
From Proto-Finnic *keski (compare Estonian kesk-), from Proto-Finno-Permic *keske (compare Northern Sami gaska, Moksha кеска (keska, “waist”), Udmurt кусып (kusyp)).

From Proto-Finnic *kesä (compare Estonian kesa (“fallow”), Veps keza (“summer”), Võro kesä (“fallow”)), from Proto-Finno-Permic *kesä (“summer”) (compare Northern Sami geassi, Erzya кизэ (kizë)), possibly a loanword from Indo-European; see it for more. Introduced into the standard language from East
From Proto-Finnic *kevät, from Proto-Finno-Permic *keŋä.
From Proto-Finnic *kiredä (compare Karelian kirie), probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *kirɜ (compare Northern Sami garas, Moksha киремс (kirems)).

From Proto-Finnic *kiskoidak (compare Estonian kiskuma), probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *kiśka- (compare Northern Sami gaikut, Moksha [script needed] (kəśkəŕams) and possibly Udmurt [script needed] (keśni̮)).
From Proto-Finnic *kickedäk, from Proto-Finno-Permic *kičke- (compare Erzya кочкомс (kočkoms, “to root out”), кочкамс (kočkams, “to choose”)).
From Proto-Finnic *koktu (compare Estonian kõht), possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *koktɜ (compare Erzya кувтёл (kuvťol, “pod, husk (seed case)”) and Udmurt кӧт (köt, “belly, stomach, body cavity”)).
From Proto-Finnic *koko (compare Estonian kogu), possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *kokᴈ (compare Eastern Mari кугу (kugu, “big”)).
From Proto-Finnic *kolmanci, from Proto-Finno-Permic *kolmamte; roughly equivalent to kolme (“three”) + -s (“-th”) (for the -a-, see the Proto-Finno-Permic entry).
From Proto-Finnic *koppala, from Proto-Finno-Permic *koppala.

parole.significato: to repair, fix, mend, remedy (restore to good working order, fix, or improve damaged condition)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *korjat'ak (compare Estonian korjama (“to collect, pick”), Votic kõrjõtõ (“to bury; to hide”)), probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *korja-.

From Proto-Finnic *koskëdak, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *koske- (compare Proto-Samic *kuoskëtēk and possibly Komi-Zyrian косны (kosny)). * (to apply to, pertain to, concern): Compare Swedish röra, beröra; perhaps a semantic loan.

parole.significato: eagle (any of several large carnivorous and carrion-eating birds in the family Accipitridae, having a powerful hooked b…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kocka (compare Estonian kotkas, Livvi kotku), from Proto-Finno-Permic *kočka (compare Northern Sami goaskin, Erzya куцькан (kućkan), Eastern Mari куткыж (kutkyž), Udmurt кыӵ (kyč)).

From Proto-Finnic *kunta (compare Estonian -kond), perhaps from Proto-Finno-Permic *kunta (compare Northern Sami goddi, Moksha кондя (kondä)); see the Proto-Finnic entry for more. The sense “municipality, commune” is based on an earlier sense “province” (= lääni, attested in 1776). In general, this

parole.significato: to weave (form a fabric or textile by passing strands of yarn or threads over and under one another, often on a loom)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kutodak (compare Estonian kuduma), from Proto-Finno-Permic *kuδa- (compare Erzya кодамс (kodams)).
From Proto-Finnic *kusa- (compare Estonian kuslapuu, Karelian kuusain), probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *kusa (compare Western Mari кузъ (kuz), Udmurt гузем-пу (guźem-pu)).

From Proto-Finnic *külmä (compare Estonian külm), probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *külmä (compare Ter Sami kallm, Erzya кельме (keľme), Eastern Mari кылме (kylme)), probably borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *gélmō.

From Proto-Finnic *kümmen, from Proto-Finno-Permic *kümme-ne (compare Erzya кемень (kemeń)). The original nominative singular form (kymmen) was replaced by the genitive singular form under the influence of kahdeksan and yhdeksän for which the nominative and genitive singular forms are also identical

parole.significato: to plough/plow, till (prepare soil for planting with a tool)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *küntädäk, from Proto-Finno-Permic *künčä- (“to dig”).

parole.significato: synonym of reikäleipä (“type of rye bread”)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kürsä, from Proto-Finno-Permic *kürsä (compare Erzya кши (kši, “bread”)).
From Proto-Finnic *küsüdäk, from Proto-Finno-Permic *küśe-w-. Compare Karelian kyšyö, Estonian küsida, Erzya кевкстемс (kevkstems) and Moksha кизефтемс (kizeftems).
From Proto-Finnic *käppä (compare Estonian käpp (“paw”)), possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *käppä (“paw, hand”) (compare Erzya кепе (kepe, “barefoot”)).

From Proto-Finnic *kärki (“black woodpecker”), from Proto-Finno-Permic *kärke (“woodpecker”). Cognates include Karelian kärki /kärgi, Võro kärgʼ (“woodpecker”), Veps kärg (“woodpecker”) and Erzya керьгата (keŕgata, “woodpecker”).
From Proto-Finnic *lehmä (“cow”) (compare Estonian lehm), from Proto-Finno-Permic *lešmä (“large domesticated animal?”) (compare Erzya лишме (lišme, “horse”)), possibly of substrate origin.
From Proto-Finnic *lisä (compare Estonian lisa, Veps liža), from Proto-Finno-Permic *lisä (compare Northern Sami lassi, Erzya лезэ (lezë, “help; benefit”)).
From Proto-Finnic *lohkët'ak (compare Ingrian loheta, Veps lohketa), equivalent to lohke- + -ta, probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *loške-.

parole.significato: charm (ability to persuade, delight or arouse admiration)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lumo, from Proto-Finno-Permic *luma- (compare Northern Sami lapmut, Eastern Mari лумаш (lumaš)).

parole.significato: to create (bring into existence out of nothing)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *loodak (compare Estonian looma), from Proto-Finno-Permic *loŋe- (“to throw, push away”) (compare Lule Sami lågŋot, Eastern Mari лоҥаш (loŋaš) and possibly Erzya лиемс (lijems, “to prepare yarn for weaving”)). Semantic development * (to throw): Original sense found already in Proto

parole.significato: to milk (to express milk from a mammal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lüpsädäk (compare Estonian lüpsma, Votic lühsä), from Proto-Finno-Permic *lüpsä- (“(to) milk”) (compare Erzya ловсо (lovso, “milk”, noun), Eastern Mari лӱшташ (lüštaš, “to milk”)).
From Proto-Finnic *majaga, from Proto-Finno-Permic *maja. Related to Veps majag and Erzya мия (mija), мияв (mijav).
From Proto-Finnic *maksadak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *maksa- (compare Erzya максомс (maksoms, “to give”)), possibly ultimately borrowed from Iranian.
From Proto-Finnic *marja (compare Estonian mari), from Proto-Finno-Permic *mërja (compare Erzya марь (maŕ), Eastern Mari мӧр (mör)).

From Proto-Finnic *mëla, from Proto-Finno-Permic *melä. Cognates include Karelian mela, Ludian mela (“oar”), Veps mela (“oar”), Estonian mõla (“paddle, oar”), Votic mõla (“paddle, oar”), Livvi mela (“paddle, oar”), Northern Sami mealli (“oar”), Erzya миле (mile, “oar, paddle”), Komi-Zyrian маль (maľ
From Proto-Finnic *meeli, from Proto-Finno-Permic *mäle. Cognates include Estonian meel, Northern Sami miella, Erzya мeль (meľ), Moksha мяль (mäľ) and Komi-Zyrian мыл (myl).
From Proto-Finnic *moni, from Proto-Finno-Permic *mone; see them for cognates and more information.
Dialectal muhku + -ra, former from Proto-Finnic *muhku, itself possibly derived from Proto-Finno-Permic *muška.

parole.significato: mute, dumb (not having the power of speech)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mükkä, from Proto-Finno-Permic *mükkä. Ultimately possibly borrowed from Proto-Indo-European *muH-ko-, compare Sanskrit मूक (muka, “mute”).
From Proto-Finnic *märehtidäk, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *märɜ-. Analyzable as märe- + -htiä.
From Proto-Finnic *nitodak (compare Estonian niduma), from Proto-Finno-Permic *ńiδa- (compare Northern Sami njađđit, Erzya недямс (neďams)).
From Proto-Finnic *nockëda (compare Ingrian notkia, Veps notked), from Proto-Finno-Permic *ńočka (“bend, curve; bent, flexible”) (compare Erzya нучкамс (nučkams, “to bend”)).
From Proto-Finnic *nocko (compare Estonian nõtk), from Proto-Finno-Permic *ńočka.

parole.significato: to tear, pull, pluck (hair, feathers, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nüktädäk (compare Veps nühtta), from Proto-Finno-Permic *ńüktä- (compare Erzya невтамс (nevtams), Eastern Mari ньыкташ (ńyktaš)).
From Proto-Finnic *nükü (compare Ingrian nyky-), from Proto-Finno-Permic *nükɜ (compare Erzya ней (nej, “now”), Komi-Zyrian нин (ńin, “already”)).
From Proto-Finnic *odottadak (compare Estonian ootama), from Proto-Finno-Permic *woča- (compare Erzya учомс (učoms), Eastern Mari вучаш (vučaš)).
From Proto-Finnic *ohi. Ultimately possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *woša (“parting, branching (of river, way)”), whence Erzya ужо (užo, “corner; angle”).

From Proto-Finnic *oikëda (compare Estonian õige), possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *wojke (“straight”) (compare Erzya виде (vide)). Semantic development * The original sense was "straight". * "straight" → "right, correct": has parallels in other languages, e.g. Latin rēctus and English right from "

parole.significato: branch, bough (woody part of a tree arising from the trunk, especially a firm one)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *oksa, from Proto-Finno-Permic *oksa. Related to Northern Sami oaksi, Eastern Mari укш (ukš).
From Proto-Finnic *oksëntadak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *okse-. Cognates include Estonian oksendama, Erzya уксномс (uksnoms), Moksha уксондомс (uksondoms) and Komi-Permyak восны (vosny).
From Proto-Finnic *onki, from Proto-Finno-Permic *oŋke, borrowed from an Indo-European language, probably Proto-Indo-Aryan *Hankás.

From Proto-Finnic *orja (“slave, servant”) (compare Estonian ori), from Proto-Finno-Permic *orja (compare Northern Sami oarji (“west”), Erzya уре (ure), Udmurt вар (var)), probably borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *áryas (“Aryan”).

parole.significato: horsefly, breezefly, gadfly, forest fly (fly of the family Tabanidae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *parma, from Proto-Finno-Permic *parma, probably onomatopoeic. Cognates include Estonian parm, Ingrian paarma, Livonian pārmaz, Veps parm, Votic paarmõz, Erzya промо (promo), пуромо (puromo) and Eastern Mari пормо (pormo).
From Proto-Finnic *pestäk, from Proto-Finno-Permic *pese- (compare Erzya пезэмс (pezëms)).

From Proto-Finnic *pihti (compare Estonian piht, Ingrian pihet pl, Karelian pihti, Veps pihthed pl, Votic pihed pl), from Proto-Finno-Permic *pište (compare Moksha [script needed] (peš), Komi-Zyrian [script needed] (peš) and Proto-Samic *pëstë, whence Northern Sami basta).

parole.significato: cloud (visible mass of water droplets suspended in the air; mass of dust, steam or smoke)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pilvi (compare Estonian pilv), from Proto-Finno-Permic *pilwe (compare Northern Sami balva, Erzya пель (peľ), Eastern Mari пыл (pyl), Udmurt пилем (piľem)). * (cloud in computing): Semantic loan from English cloud.

parole.significato: drop (a small mass of liquid, just large enough to hold its own round shape)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pisara (compare Estonian pisar (“tear”)), possibly derived from Proto-Finno-Permic *pića- (“to rain, drizzle”) (compare Erzya пиземе (pizeme, “rain”)).

From Proto-Finnic *pistädäk (compare Estonian pistma), from Proto-Finno-Permic *pistä- (compare Eastern Mari пышташ (pyštaš)). * (to put, tuck, stick): Compare Swedish sticka, German stecken, English stick on the one hand, and Eastern Mari [script needed] (pə̑štem) on the other.

From Proto-Finnic *pitädäk (compare Estonian pidama), from Proto-Finno-Permic *pitä- (compare Erzya педямс (peďams, “to get stuck”), Eastern Mari [script needed] (pə̂ze-, “to hold”)). * (to hold (an event, etc.)): Compare Swedish hålla, English hold. * (to consider, regard): Compare German halten, S

parole.significato: anther (pollen-bearing part of the stamen of a flower)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ponci, from Proto-Finno-Permic *ponte or Proto-Uralic *ponče (“tail”).

From Proto-Finnic *porcas (compare Estonian põrsas), from Proto-Finno-Permic *porćas (compare Erzya пурцос (purcos), Udmurt [script needed] (parś), unless these are separate borrowings), borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *porśos (> *párśas) (ultimately cognate with English pork).
From Proto-Finnic *pocka, from Proto-Finno-Permic *počka.

parole.significato: to dismantle, dissemble, take apart, disassemble, deconstruct (into pieces; possibly with osiin (“into parts”) for clar…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *purkadak, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *purka- (compare Northern Sami borgádit, Erzya порксамс (porksams)).
From Proto-Finnic *pühä (compare Estonian püha), from Proto-Finno-Permic *pišä ~ *püšä (compare Northern Sami bassi, Erzya пежеть (pežeť, “sin”), Udmurt пож (pož, “dirty, foul”)).

From Proto-Finnic *pisüdäk (compare Estonian püsima, Veps püžuda), from Proto-Finno-Permic *pise-w- (compare Erzya пезнамс (peznams, “to pierce; to stick”), Moksha пезомс (pezoms), Eastern Mari пижа́ш (pižáš)), with the second-syllable -y- causing labialization of the initial -i- to -y-.
From Proto-Finnic *rahko, from Proto-Finno-Permic *raška-w.
From Proto-Finnic *rasëda, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *ranśe.

From Proto-Finnic *repoi, from Proto-Finno-Permic *repä (compare Erzya ривезь (riveź)), borrowed from early Indo-Iranian (compare Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hrawpāćás, Sanskrit लोपि (lopi), Persian روباه (rubâh); Germanic terms like Swedish räv are probably parallel borrowings from Indo-Iranian).

parole.significato: A traditional northern European (Fennoscandian and Russian) grain drying and threshing cabin, in which the grain was dr…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *riihi, from Proto-Finno-Permic *riŋeše, itself possibly a Wanderwort. Cognates include Estonian rehi, Karelian riihi. Swedish ria and Latvian rija are borrowings from Finnic.

parole.significato: vent, flap (especially one located near the ceiling for ventilation purposes)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *räppänä, from Proto-Finno-Permic *räppä; compare Karelian reppänä. Cognates include Lule Sami riehpen.
From Proto-Finnic *sarni (compare Livonian sǟrna), from Proto-Finno-Permic *särńä (compare Eastern Mari шертне (šertńe), Western Mari шӓртньы (šärtńy)).
From Proto-Finnic *sakëda, from Proto-Finno-Permic *sake.

parole.significato: strait, sound (narrow channel of water connecting two larger bodies of water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *salmi (compare Estonian salm), from Proto-Finno-Permic *ćalme (compare Northern Sami čoalbmi and possibly Udmurt сюм (śum, “bay, cove”)). Doublet of jolma (which is a Sami loan).

parole.significato: series (number of things that follow on one after the other)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sarja (“lath board, row of laths; row, bunch”), from Proto-Finno-Permic *śarja (“lath, batten, bar”). Adopted as an equivalent to Latin series in the literary language based on the original meanings "row, bunch" and the sense related to chicken eggs listed below which can also be

From Proto-Finnic *sauvu (compare Livonian so’v), possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *śëwwe (“smoke”) (compare Northern Sami suovva and possibly Erzya сув (suv, “fog, curtain”)). * (unit of taxation): Originally defined based on the number of residential buildings with a chimney. Compare Swedish rök,

parole.significato: back (the rear of the body, especially the part between the neck and the end of the spine and opposite the chest and be…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *selkä (compare Estonian selg), from Proto-Finno-Permic *śelkä (compare Proto-Samic *čielkē, Eastern Mari шӹлӹж (šÿlÿž, “area of the sacrum”)).
From Proto-Finnic *seppä, from Proto-Finno-Permic *śeppä (“skilled”).

siem- + -aista, from the rare dialectal word siemi, from Proto-Finnic *seemi (compare derivations Estonian sõõm (“gulp”), Livonian sēmḑa (“milk”)), from Proto-Finno-Permic *śäme- (compare Erzya симемс (simems, “to drink”)).
From Proto-Finnic *sikedä, from Proto-Finno-Permic *śikɜ (“thick, dense, solid”). Related to Erzya сееде (sejede, “frequent; dense”).
From Proto-Finnic *sini, from Proto-Finno-Permic *sine. Cognates include Erzya сэнь (sëń).

parole.significato: inner, internal, interior, inward, inside; indoor; inland
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sicä (compare Estonian sise-), from Proto-Finno-Permic *śićä (compare Moksha сезем (sezem, “heartwood”)).

From Proto-Finnic *solki, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *śolke. Related to Erzya сюлгамо (śulgamo). However, the cognates outside Finnic are not entirely regular, which makes the etymology beyond Proto-Finnic uncertain.
From Proto-Finnic *sonta, from Proto-Finno-Permic *śonta. Cognate with Estonian sõnnik and Western Mari шандӹ (šandÿ).

parole.significato: gravel (small fragments of rock, technical definition: soil with rocks predominantly with a size between 2 and 20, or e…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *cora (compare Estonian sõra), from Proto-Finno-Permic *ćora (“grain”) (compare Erzya сюро (śuro, “grain”)), borrowing from early Proto-Balto-Slavic *śoros.

parole.significato: finger (one of the five extremities of the hand)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sormi, from Proto-Finno-Permic *sorme. Cognates include Estonian sõrm, Northern Sami suorbma, Erzya сур (sur).

parole.significato: to close, shut (a door, gate, box, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sulkëdak (compare Estonian sulgema), from Proto-Finno-Permic *śulke- (compare Erzya and Moksha сёлгомс (śolgoms, “to close”)).

parole.significato: shank (lower part of the leg); shin and calf
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sääri, from Proto-Finno-Permic *ćäŋäre.
From Proto-Finnic *säski (compare Estonian sääsk, Veps säsk), from Proto-Finno-Permic *ćëćke ~ *ćäćke (compare Northern Sami čuoika, Erzya сеське (seśke), Moksha сяське (säśke)).

parole.significato: grindstone (abrasive wheel for sharpening, polishing or grinding)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tahko (compare Estonian tahk, Ingrian tahko, Veps tahk), from Proto-Finno-Permic *taškɜ ~ *tašɜ ~ *tuškɜ (compare Komi-Zyrian тыш (tyš), Udmurt тыш (tyš), Eastern Mari тош (toš)), perhaps of substrate origin.

parole.significato: oak (any tree or shrub of the genus Quercus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tammi (compare Estonian tamm, Karelian tammi, Livonian täm), from Proto-Finno-Permic *tamme (compare Erzya тумо (tumo), Eastern Mari тумо (tumo)), possibly ultimately of substrate origin.
From Proto-Finnic *tankëda, from Proto-Finno-Permic *taŋketa.
From Proto-Finnic *terä, from Proto-Finno-Permic *terä.
From Proto-Finnic *tee, from Proto-Finno-Permic *teje.

parole.significato: can bring oneself (to do), to dare ((to) do), venture (to do), have the nerve (to do)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tohtidak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *tošte-.

From Proto-Finnic *tuho, probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *tukšɜ-. Cognates include Ingrian tuho, Votic tuho, Veps tuho, Veps tuhoze (“astray”, adverb) and possibly Udmurt [script needed] (tiš, “bloody battle”).

parole.significato: hair (cover of hair on a human head); head of hair
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tukka, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *čukka.

parole.significato: flood (overflow of a large amount of water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tulva (cognate with Karelian tulva), possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *tulwa (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).

parole.significato: muzzle (protruding part of an ungulate's head)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *turpa, from Proto-Finno-Permic *turpa. Cognates include Erzya турва (turva, “lip”), Moksha търва (tərva, “lip”), Western Mari тӱрвӧ (türvö, “lip”), Udmurt тырпы (tyrpy, “lip”), and Komi-Permyak тырп (tyrp, “lip”).

From Proto-Finnic *tuuli (compare Estonian tuul), from Proto-Finno-Permic *towle (compare Western Mari [script needed] (tul, “storm”), Udmurt тӧл (töl, “wind”), Eastern Mansi [script needed] (tol, “cloud”)).

parole.significato: work, toil, effort, labour (effort expended on a particular task)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *töö (compare Estonian töö, Livonian tīe, Votic tüü), from Proto-Finno-Permic *tewe (compare Erzya тев (tev)).

parole.significato: ear (fruiting body of a grain plant)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tähkä, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *teškä ~ *tekšä ~ *täškä (compare Erzya тикше (tikše, “grass”), Komi-Permyak тош (toš), Udmurt туш (tuš)), perhaps of substrate origin.
From Proto-Finnic *tähti, from Proto-Finno-Permic *täštä. Cognate to Karelian tähti, Estonian täht and Erzya теште (tešte). Sense 4 is a semantic loan from English star.
From Proto-Finnic *täti (compare Estonian tädi, Veps täti), ultimately probably from baby talk. Possibly already in Proto-Finno-Permic *tätä (compare Moksha тядя (tädä, “mother”)).
From Proto-Finnic *ulko (compare Estonian ulgu-), from Proto-Finno-Permic *ulka (compare Northern Sami olgu, Komi-Zyrian ылö (ylö, “far”)).
From Proto-Finnic *uni, from Proto-Finno-Permic *une. Cognates include Erzya он (on), Western Mari ом (om).
From Proto-Finnic *up'ot'ak, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *uppa (“suffocating”). If so, related to Erzya and Moksha опа (opa, “warm, hot, stuffy, suffocating”).

parole.significato: track, groove, rut, trail, furrow (mark in the form of a groove or long, narrow depression left by something that has p…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ura, from Proto-Finno-Permic *ura. Related to Karelian ura, Udmurt [script needed] (i̮ri̮-). * (career): A semantic loan from some other European language, compare French carrière (“racecourse, career”), from Medieval Latin carrāria (“path for carts”).
From Proto-Finnic *urgët'ak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *urke-. Cognates include Livonian urgõ and Erzya оргодемс (orgodems).

From Proto-Finnic *udar (compare Estonian udar (“udder”), Livvi udareh (“udder”)), from Proto-Finno-Permic *utare (compare Erzya одар (odar, “udder”)), borrowed from an Indo-Iranian language (compare Sanskrit ऊधर् (ūdhar)), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ówHdʰr̥ (“udder”).
From Proto-Finnic *uurtadak, probably derived from Proto-Finno-Permic *owre (“groove”).

parole.significato: maple (any tree of the genus Acer)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vahtëra, from Proto-Finno-Permic [Term?]. Cognate with Estonian vaher, Ingrian vaaher, Karelian voahteri, Livonian vǭ’dõr, Veps vahtaŕ, Votic vaahtõrõ, Erzya укштор (ukštor), Moksha уштор (uštor) and Eastern Mari ваштар (vaštar).

parole.significato: Finnish span (distance between the thumb and the index finger)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vaksa, from Proto-Finno-Permic *waksa. Cognates include Erzya вакс (vaks).

parole.significato: phase, stage, step (distinct or distinguishable part of a sequence or process)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vajëh (“gap”) (compare Estonian vahe), probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *waješ.

parole.significato: to cast, mold/mould (make a cast by pouring into a mold/mould)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *valadak (compare Estonian valama), from Proto-Finno-Permic *wala- ~ *wälä- (compare Moksha валомс (valoms, “to pour; to wet”), Eastern Mari велаш (velaš, “to spill”)).

parole.significato: a staff with a hook at one end; used as a tool for turning over logs in slash-and-burn cultivation
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vanko (cognate with Estonian vang and Võro vang), from Proto-Finno-Permic *waŋka, probably borrowed from Indo-Iranian (compare Sanskrit वङ्क (vaṅka, “crooked”)).

parole.significato: A long, narrow, (relatively) straight part of something:
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *varci (compare Estonian vars), probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *warte (compare Eastern Mari вурдо (vurdo)).

parole.significato: fawn, calf (of e.g. a deer, elk or antelope)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vasa (compare Ludian vaza), from Proto-Finno-Permic *wasa (compare Inari Sami vyesi, Erzya ваз (vaz)), borrowed from Proto-Iranian *wacáh (“yearling calf”) (compare Digor Ossetian уӕс (wæs)).
From Proto-Finnic *vasara, from Proto-Finno-Permic *waśara (compare Erzya узере (uzere)), borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wáȷ́ras (compare Sanskrit वज्र (vájra)).

From Proto-Finnic *vasta (compare Estonian vast, Livonian vastõ, Votic vassõ), from Proto-Finno-Permic *wasta (“a place opposite or across”) (compare Northern Sami vuostá (“towards, against”), Erzya вастомс (vastoms, “to meet”), Moksha васта (vasta, “spot, place”), Eastern Mari ваштареш (vaštareš, “

From Proto-Finnic *vehnä (compare Ingrian vehnä), from Proto-Finno-Permic *wešnä (“spelt, wheat”) (compare Erzya виш (viš, “spelt”)), perhaps of substrate origin. Introduced into the standard language from Eastern Finnish in the 19th century, replacing the Western Finnish word nisu.

From Proto-Finnic *veneh (compare Estonian vene), from Proto-Finno-Permic *weneš (compare Erzya венч (venč)). The word is attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552), but was originally mainly characteristic of the eastern as well as Ostrobothnian dialects.

parole.significato: to stretch (become longer by stretching, or by being pulled)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *venüdäk (compare Estonian venima), from Proto-Finno-Permic *wene-w- (compare Northern Sami vatnat, Erzya венемемс (venemems), Eastern Mari вийнаш (vijnaš)).
From Proto-Finnic *vero, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *werᴈ. Cognate to Karelian vero, and possibly Votic vero and Veps vero.

parole.significato: side, edge (region immediately next to something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *veeri, from Proto-Finno-Permic *wäre. Akin to Estonian veer, Northern Sami vierra (“ridge”) and Erzya вере (vere, “upside”), вирь (viŕ, “forest”).

From Proto-Finnic *viha (compare Estonian viha), from Proto-Finno-Permic *wiša (compare Northern Sami vašši, Udmurt вож (vož, “hate”), Komi-Zyrian веж (vež, “envy”)), borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wišás.

parole.significato: oblique, askew, crooked, diagonal, skew, lopsided
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vino, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *wińa (compare Ter Sami [script needed] (va̭nnai̭jᵃ), Erzya венежа (veneža)).

parole.significato: little, few, scarce (low in number or amount)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vähä (compare Estonian vähe, Votic vähä), from Proto-Finno-Permic *wäšä (compare Erzya вишка (viška, “little”), веженсь (veženś, “youngest”)).

From Proto-Finnic *äijä (compare Karelian äijä (“a lot, great, tall, many”), Veps äi (“a lot”)), from Proto-Finno-Permic *äjjä (compare Northern Sami áddjá (“old male relative”), Erzya оя (oja, “friend”), Udmurt айы (ajy, “father, male”)).
